title: What's more shameful for a game dev: using AI, or using AI and being too scared to admit it?
author: Parking-Screen7233
selftext:
Let's be honest. A lot of devs are using AI right now. For code, for placeholder art, for translations, for brainstorming, for that one shader they couldn't figure out at 3 AM.

And a lot of them will swear on their Steam page that they don't.

Using a tool isn't shameful. We've always used tools. Engines, asset packs, middleware, free fonts, Stack Overflow. Nobody makes 100% of a game alone, and nobody pretends to.

What is shameful is lying to the people who pay for your game. Hiding it because you're afraid of the comment section. Letting your players believe something that isn't true just to dodge a few angry replies.

If you used AI, own it. Say what you used it for and what you made yourself. Let players decide with real information. If your game is good, it will stand. If it isn't, hiding your tools won't save it.

Using AI is a choice. Lying about it is a character flaw.

So, which one would you rather be called out for?

comments.author: PaintingThat7623
comments.body:
<rolls eyes>

AI is the standard tool for gamedev. Get over it.

replies.author: TechgeekOne
replies.body: Very much this. A tool is a tool. People are attaching _way_ too much emotional baggage to which tools they use now simply because it's AI.

replies.author: PaintingThat7623
replies.body:
I've just read a reddit thread where a guy was advertising his very unoriginal game. His main selling point? "I didn't use AI!". How long it took? 8 months full time.

I'm not linking this, but this game looks like something I'd do in a week with AI. I don't know why people are so averse and want to keep using a hammer when an automatic, laser drill has been invented.

replies.author: TechgeekOne
replies.body: 8 months sounds about right for that if going by old time estimates. I've spent up to 8 months just building part of a larger system before. But also like, why would I torture myself with that now? AI can do a bunch of the work at equivalent quality (when guided properly) in a fraction of the time and then I can focus on the other more important thing of finishing the project.

replies.author: Parking-Screen7233
replies.body: I think it’s better to be honest than to get caught.

replies.author: AcceptableArm8841
replies.body: I would rather not get harassed and have death threats. Thanks

comments.author: Sch4k4l
comments.body:
There’s no shame in using a tool that makes the work easier and improves the end result.

Yes, the resource consumption resulting from reckless, wasteful use of AI is a significant problem, as are all the political and economic issues associated with it.

But hiding the truth... or even lying... won’t help anyone in the long run. I’ve experienced firsthand what it’s like when a mob of anti-AI users descends on a Reddit thread and downvotes all my comments in multiple rounds of discussion, simply to really give the “AI user” a hard time. They don’t care that they’ve caused real problems for my young Reddit account in the process. They just want to push their fanatical ideology. That’s how it is with all extremists.

But back to your question: lying and hiding is definitely the worse choice.

I just hope that in 6 to 9 months, people will slowly get used to AI usage and finally come back to reality and the present.

Have a great day!

replies.author: Parking-Screen7233
replies.body: I have never seen a boycott as unreasonable as this one. I wonder—do these people themselves use AI in their own lives, for instance to look up information or edit personal photos?

replies.author: Warsel77
replies.body:
The odd thing: people often cite environmental reasons why they hate AI (CO2 emissions or equivalents thereof) but the meat industry globally has a factor 34 times MORE output than all (AI and not AI) server farms in the world.

I am not a vegetarian and I do not think we should ignore one problem because there is a bigger one, but the selective outrage over one thing while accepting another much worse thing is somewhat interesting.

replies.author: Sch4k4l
replies.body:
With a statement like that, though, you’ll make twice as many enemies.

But thematically, you’re absolutely right, and if you seriously weigh the pros and cons:

when it comes to the question "Meat or AI?"

it would be beneficial for humanity to leave meat consumption behind and improve our quality of life with AI.

But those are just half-baked ideas :)

replies.author: Warsel77
replies.body: sure, don't we all thrive on half-baked ideas here on reddit? :)

comments.author: thirsty_pretzelzz
comments.body:
I agree it’s not shameful and it’s honestly such a blurry spectrum at this point, with how many common tools have some level of ai support in them. 

An issue though is last I saw, say if you declare on steam that you had ai help you with some code, (which let’s be real, the majority of devs do at this point) you then get the same big ai use label as someone who used gen ai for all their art (which hey fine too if that’s your thing) sure there are more details provided by the dev once the user reads further but many people, soon as they see that ai declaration text, they already assume the worst and you get lumped in all together and the user has moved on

replies.author: Parking-Screen7233
replies.body: Extremists will fixate on that one minor flaw to pass judgment on the entire game; I find that quite sad, but acknowledging it brings me a far greater sense of relief than trying to hide it.

comments.author: alanbdee
comments.body: Not actually playing the stuff your AI agent wrote.

comments.author: Almaravarion
comments.body:
I wonder if You realize that Steam disclosure requires disclosure of any user-facing generative AI.  
Brainstorming, code generation do not fit the requirement. Therefore if someone used it for either, would not need to disclose it just for doing those things.

My personal stance on AI use in my project is:  
I used AI, I am using AI and I WILL use AI, if You've got problem with that, go elsewhere, if You whine about tool use you can go F yourself.

Expecting however ANY use of AI during development process and calling not disclosure of AI use outside of disclosure's scope 'lying' is reaction of a whiny child, rather than someone who understands what the disclosure is, and what is its scope.

Not going out of your way to confess every single action one made during design, to pray for absolution of angry mob for what is not, and should not, be considered a design sin, is not 'lying', regardless of Your delusions.

Making crap quality product - THAT is something to criticize. Tool selection? Should not be of any concern to consumer, the same way as I'd be willing to complain someone did a shit job painting a wall, but not for use of e.g. dynamite or a toothbrush, as long as end quality is acceptable.

comments.author: Pleasant_Salt6810
comments.body: what's the value of a game? it's how it plays, how it's feel, not how it's made, nobody cares how a thing is made as long as it works? People who pay for a game cares about how the gameplay is, not how it's made, so what it's so shameful?

replies.author: Parking-Screen7233
replies.body: Posts railing against AI are flooding Reddit, I’d bet you’ll come across them in any group related to indie games.

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: Instead of shaming devs who hide AI use ( I don't) you should be shaming AI haters that hate a game solely on the fact it uses AI, do review bombing, etc. It is ok to not like something, it is not ok to harass someone for it.

replies.author: Parking-Screen7233
replies.body: Game critics—the very gatekeepers who connect games to players—are often the harshest detractors; such criticism is inherently controversial and provides them with a veneer of moral righteousness. Yet, this dynamic leaves independent game developers feeling fearful, anxious, and compelled to keep their true sentiments hidden.

comments.author: GamingAllZTime
comments.body:
Most supply chains involve child labor.

People boycott stuff made by AI, but conviently find reasons they "have" to consume child labor.

comments.author: Economy_Bedroom3902
comments.body:
I don't think using AI should be shameful.  In the non-game software development world, AI is just the expected norm.  It's actually weird how isolated game dev communities have been able to keep themselves in many cases.

Using AI will be a virtually universal normal part of creative work sooner or later, Even if anti-AI advocates win all their lawsuits and get all kinds of changes and concessions on behalf of AI copywrite etc, the cat is not going back into the bag.  There will still be a version of this more locked down, conservative, restricted, that becomes a normal part of every creative/coding workflow.  You're probably at an advantage learning it now rather than waiting for it to be a mandatory skill on every job application.

Don't pretend you aren't using AI when you are.  Dishonest behavior is far more likely to cost you than get you ahead in the end.

Where I can see shame being relevant:  Are you using AI to quickly clone other new releases so you can get a cut of the pie they earned through hard work?  Are you using AI to dodge copyright or trademark issues (my characters all look like mickey mouse, but it's not my fault cause an AI made them that way).  Are you using AI to attempt to eliminate the employment of other developers?

Those are all ethnically questionable things whether or not there are current legal loopholes for them.  Feel free to feel shame for those activities!

comments.author: Warsel77
comments.body:
>What is shameful is lying to the people who pay for your game. Hiding it because you're afraid of the comment section. Letting your players believe something that isn't true just to dodge a few angry replies.

What is shameful is the witch-hunt that is currently pulled off around using AI.

You may like AI or your may not, but the amount of hatred that is spewed towards people who declare AI use is unproportional. And that's exactly the reason.

The idea that a consumer in 2026 can somehow control that they only buy non-AI products is unrealistic. Everyone (including reddit!) is using AI. Bashing that solo developer who tries to please everyone is just bullying.
